extraction.name: TravelPlanner
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating language agents in tool-use and complex planning within multiple constraints, focusing on travel planning scenarios. It provides a rich sandbox environment with various tools for accessing nearly four million data records, and 1,225 meticulously curated planning intents and reference plans.
extraction.creator: Jian Xie, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, Yu Su
extraction.publisher: Fudan University, The Ohio State University, The Pennsylvania State University, Meta AI
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was constructed through a multi-step pipeline: 1) Environment setup with static databases containing nearly 4 million data entries crawled from the Internet, 2) Diverse travel query design with randomly chosen elements (departure city, destination, date range) adjusted for complexity, 3) Human annotation by 20 graduate students who meticulously annotated 1,225 query-plan pairs, and 4) Quality control through detailed author review of every query and plan.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of approximately 4 million data entries crawled from the Internet, organized into databases for six different tools: CitySearch (312 entries), FlightSearch (3,827,361 entries), DistanceMatrix (17,603 entries), RestaurantSearch (9,552 entries), AttractionSearch (5,303 entries), and AccommodationSearch (5,064 entries). Some data is derived from publicly available data on the Internet.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Planning intents and reference plans were meticulously curated. Key components (transportation, restaurants, attractions, and accommodations) were extracted from natural language and organized into formally structured plans for evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Plans were evaluated automatically through pre-defined scripts across multiple dimensions including Delivery Rate, Commonsense Constraint Pass Rate, Hard Constraint Pass Rate, and Final Pass Rate. Two evaluation strategies were used: micro (ratio of passed constraints to total constraints) and macro (ratio of plans passing all constraints).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4-Turbo was used for extracting key components from natural language plans.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark presents significant challenges with current language agents achieving very low success rates. The evaluation criteria are based on authors' consensus regarding commonsense, acknowledging that definitions of commonsense may vary.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: TravelPlanner aims to provide an effective benchmark for complex planning in future research and contribute to the development of language agents with human-level cognitive capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is divided into training, validation, and test sets. Training set (45 pairs with human-annotated plans) can be used for evaluation feedback and reinforcement learning techniques. Validation and test sets are strictly for evaluation only, with cheating prohibited.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors will release evaluation scripts to foster innovation and aid development of new methods.
